newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan party leaders to seal loose alliance.
newsitem.headline: Japan party leaders to seal loose alliance.

text.p: The partners in Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's outgoing coalition will announce an agreement on Thursday to establish an out-of-cabinet alliance in place of a coalition framework, political sources said.

Officials from the smallest member of the outgoing coalition, the Sakigake Party, said Hashimoto would meet Social Democratic Party leader Takako Doi and Sakigake head Akiko Domoto later in the day to formally launch the alliance along with a package of policy goals.

In general elections earlier this month, Hashimoto's conservative Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) failed to clinch a majority in parliament, finishing 12 seats short of a majority in the decisive Lower House.

The LDP's two old allies, however, refused to renew the coalition, fearing they would become irrelevant partners in an LDP-dominated bloc, but agreed to set up a standing committee outside the cabinet to fine-tune policy issues.
Although the LDP is short of a majority, Hashimoto is assured of re-election as prime minister when parliament convenes on November 7 because of the party's strength in parliament's two chambers.

The agreement includes a timetable for reforms of the bloated central government bureaucracy as a whole, as well as specific measures covering the Finance Ministry and the Bank of Japan, Sakigake sources said.
Other reforms include the establishment of a civil service watchdog group in parliament and a body to review the controversial sales tax, which is due to be raised in April.
The agreement also calls for a reduction in parliamentary seats and the enactment of bills to introduce a public nursing system for the aged and to encourage volunteer work.

The document will also list items on which the parties have failed to reach agreement, including a proposed ban on political donations from private firms and a reduction of U.S. troops stationed on Japan's southern island of Okinawa.
